## 1. What this block is, in one sentence

**This is the block in which two sheets arrive in the ordinary post and are read out loud in a room at the high end of that market street, and the first of them says that people with a warrant and about nine others went up about nine hundred yards of a stair at about the sixth hour on a named morning and that the gate at the top of that stair is held and the people on it are not leaving, and the second, eleven days later, says the upper terraces are out of the hands of the men who held them and the place is still held from below and the central engine is damaged and one man has gone down into the lower archive and has not come out, AND THE SURRENDER THE SERIES OWED THIS VOLUME IS SPENT AS ONE LINE ON ONE OF THOSE TWO SHEETS, AND THE FINDING IS THAT A PLACE IS STILL OCCUPIED AND ITS CENTRAL ENGINE IS DAMAGED AND A VICTORY CANNOT BE PRESERVED BY ONE PERSON, AND THAT ABOUT FOUR HUNDRED PEOPLE IN NINE COUNTIES HAVE BEEN READING ABOUT IT FOR FOUR MONTHS AND NINE HUNDRED PEOPLE ALONG ELEVEN MILES OF MADE ROAD STILL HAVE NOT HEARD IT.** It is also the block that **prints no System panel at all, because the volume's one was spent at `chapter-0825.md` in Batch 0003 and may not be spent again**, that carries the twenty-eighth first of a month in a row on a Sunday that is not a market morning and on which the practice therefore runs, that spends the last of the volume's six names, and that ends the volume on the twenty-fifth of Rainmonth YR 324, a Wednesday, six days before the first of Harvestmonth, with a floor, a lamp, a number said twice in the dark by two people who are not him, and a sheet of paper with nine lines on it and no names and no seal.

## 4. What the block must contain

**THE VOLUME'S CLIMAX HAPPENED AND IT WAS NOT SEEN AND NOBODY IN THIS COUNTY SAW ANY OF IT AND NO CHAPTER OF THIS BLOCK ENTERS IT.** **`outline/volume-17.md` §9 is the whole of this and it is not softened by anything in this file: nobody in this county is in it, the paper that says so arrives in the ordinary post, and the man of thirty-two with a stick is four days off on a made road when it does.** **Everything that happens in either place is reported in the ordinary post and read out in a room, exactly as Volume 16 reported the gate coming off its hinges, and THE OMISSION IS A DECISION AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT AND A SUCCESSOR MAY NOT CURE IT IN VOLUME 18 BY GOING THERE.** No chapter of this block enters that place, puts anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair, or shows what is on the far side of the ninth of the nine stones.

**THE FIRST SHEET, AND IT IS ONE SHEET IN THE ORDINARY POST AND IT IS NOT THE ROLL AND IT IS NOT THE SHEET ALREADY NAILED UP.** It comes up that made road on a Crown's cart with two satchels under the seat and a driver who does not know what is in them and is not asked and does not ask. It says that **at about the sixth hour on a named morning, people with a Crown's warrant and about nine others, among them people who used to sit in that office four hundred miles off, went up about nine hundred yards of a stair, and that the gate at the top of that stair is held and the people on it are not leaving.** **IT MAY BE READ OUT ONCE, IN A ROOM, BY A CARTER, AND THE ROOM MAY BE THE ROOM OVER THAT WEIGH-HOUSE OR A ROOM IN THE INN AT THE HIGH END OF THAT MARKET STREET OR A ROOM HIRED FOR IT, and about nine people hear all of it and about five do not, and NOBODY ASKS HIM TO READ IT AGAIN.** **IT IS NOT A THIRD COPY OF ANYTHING AND IT IS NOT NAILED UP ON THAT FRAME, and the count of things on that frame stays five and the count of questions on it stays three, and a writer who wants to nail it up is writing the wrong chapter.**

**THE SECOND SHEET, ELEVEN DAYS AFTER THE FIRST, AND THE ELEVEN DAYS ARE ON THE PAGE.** It says **the upper terraces are out of the hands of the men who held them, and the place is still held from below, and the central engine is damaged, and one man has gone down into the lower archive and has not come out.** **THE DAMAGE IS NOT A VICTORY AND IS NOT CURABLE IN THIS VOLUME AND IS NOT ANYBODY'S ACHIEVEMENT, AND THE MAN IN THE LOWER ARCHIVE IS NOT FOUND AND IS NOT BROUGHT OUT AND IS NOT TOLD ABOUT.** The second sheet is also read out once and nobody asks for it again.

**THE SURRENDER, AND IT IS SPENT AS ONE LINE ON ONE OF THOSE TWO SHEETS, AND IT IS NOT THE ANTAGONIST'S.** **`outline/series.md`'s antagonist ladder owes this volume one surrender, being the Warden whose name stands third in that ladder, and that ladder is fixed and is not softened by this file.** **THE LINE ON THE SHEET MAY CARRY HER NAME, because a document is where a name in this project goes and a mouth is where it does not, AND THE NARRATION AND THE PROSE OF EVERY CHAPTER OF THIS BLOCK REFERS TO HER BY HER OFFICE AND NOT BY HER NAME, so that no name out of this volume's six is spent on a woman who has not been on the page in about eleven volumes.** **THE LADDER SAYS SHE IS TRIED, and the block may say that she is to be tried, and it may not say how the trial goes, and it may not end the trial, and it may not put her in a room.** **A WRITER WHO INVENTS A NEW NAME FOR HER, OR WHO GIVES THE SURRENDER TO ANYBODY ELSE, OR WHO MAKES THE SURRENDER THE ENDING OF THE SERIES, HAS LEFT THE LADDER.**

**THE RESOLUTION IS WHAT `outline/volume-17.md` §10 GIVES AND NONE OF IT IS A RESCUE.** **The place is still occupied and held from below, and the central engine is damaged, and one man is in the lower archive and has not come out, and nobody in this county saw any of it, and no chapter of this volume enters it, and the occupation is not ended. A victory cannot be preserved by one person and this block says so on the page in about nine hundred words or fewer. THIS COUNTY'S CONTRIBUTION IS NINE TRADES ON NINE LINES OF A PAPER WITH NO SEAL ON IT AND NO NAME ON ANY OF THEM.** The offer is refused and the refusal is not published, the paper the refusal would have gone on is the paper this county is copying by hand, and about nine hundred people along eleven miles of made road have not heard either thing. Nobody in this county is a delegate and nobody here has been asked to be one.

**THE NAME THIS BLOCK MAY SPEND IS `Prue Sillick` AND IT IS THE LAST OF THE VOLUME'S SIX.**

**THE FOURTH RULED HEAD IS STILL EMPTY AT EVERY ONE OF THE TEN DATELINES AND NO FIFTH HEAD IS RULED ON ANY OF THEM**, and the register still holds ten questions with no finding under any of them, and the day-book still stands at eleven entries, and the copyist of about twenty-six rules no head and is told about none of it, and the press stands open with no date on it, and the leaf at the back of the day-book carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody, and the four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing. **The four copied pages are on the top shelf of that press above the half leaf and are not resolved and nobody has asked who wrote them.** **Nothing about the practice, the ten things, the four lines of chalk, the three answers of Batch 0001, this volume's first three, Batch 0003's refusal, the sheet, the hand paper, the seal, the bleed, the re-anchoring, the two sheets of this block, the surrender or the name of this block goes into any document in this volume, and the name given at a stall in a market street goes into no document of any kind.**

## 5. The ending of the block, and of the volume

**A completed beat, not a cliffhanger cut in the middle of a sentence, and not a rescue.** **THE LAST LINE OF THE NARRATIVE IS A FLOOR, A LAMP, A NUMBER SAID TWICE IN THE DARK BY TWO PEOPLE WHO ARE NOT HIM, AND A SHEET OF PAPER WITH NINE LINES ON IT AND NO NAMES AND NO SEAL**, being `outline/volume-17.md` §10 item six, **and that paragraph is followed by the cost coda and then by the closing money column, so it is not the last line of the file, and a writer may not print it as the last line of the volume without naming the two paragraphs that come after it.** **THE VOLUME ENDS ON THE TWENTY-FIFTH OF RAINMONTH YR 324, A WEDNESDAY, SIX DAYS BEFORE THE FIRST OF HARVESTMONTH, which is the fourth running volume to end on the twenty-fifth of a month and the second to end on a Wednesday.**

At that last dateline, and every figure derived from day 3180 and none copied out of a row: **the low room at the back of that office was open on four market mornings of this volume and about nine people were inside it on each, and the drawer eleven inches deep was not opened once in two hundred and nine days and the county's one seal and its ribbon and a set of standard weights are still in it, and nobody was asked what a seal is for.** Nobody went up the cart track and the nine hurdles are still across it and the thumb of lime on the shoe of the top one is gone to powder and the last lime cart was five hundred and fifty-two days ago and the road behind the hurdles has been shut five hundred and thirty-three days. **The sheet on the frame is a fifth thing beside three copies of a roll and its date is one hundred and forty-six days past and the fourth line is empty on all three copies and the roll is three hundred and fifty-three days on that frame and is not filled in and not taken down and not torn up.** This county's copy of the hand paper still has nine lines on it and a trade on each and no name on any and no seal on it, and nobody in nine counties has been asked whose trade is on any of its nine lines. The four lines of chalk are under the hood where the rain does not reach and are still four and are still not writing. The register holds ten questions and gains no entry, no fifth head is ruled, the fourth ruled head is empty, the day-book stands at eleven entries, and the leaf at the back of it carries nine figures and a date and the names of nobody. **Nobody in this county is a delegate and nobody here has been asked to be one, and a place nine days off is still held from below with its central engine damaged and one man in a lower archive who has not come out, and this county's contribution to about four hundred papers is nine trades and no names and no seal.**

**`outline/volume-17.md` §16 item 6's three promises are CARRIED OUT UNCONDUCTED AND NONE OF THEM MAY BE BROKEN IN THIS BLOCK:** no chapter of this block enters that place or puts anybody on about nine hundred yards of a stair or shows what is on the far side of the ninth of the nine stones; no consent of any sealed community is obtained, asked for, received or inferred, and the half leaf stays face down and no head is filled or ruled; and the roll is not filled, no name goes against any road, no road is shut on the strength of any paper, none of the three copies is taken down or torn up, no hurdle is lifted, no bar is tried, nobody goes up that cart track, the ninth yard does not start, the mallet is not picked up, and **the drawer at the back of that office is not opened.**

**`state/continuity.md` 1859 and `state/open-threads.md` 802 carry one warning forward and a successor may not learn the opposite of it:** four lines on a sill are not the beginning of a cure, a page in a woman's hand is not a cure, a sentence in an unclaimed hand on a folded sheet is not a cure, **a bleed that has not faded in two hundred and sixty days is not a cure, AND TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTY IS THIS BLOCK'S OWN FIGURE AT ITS LAST DATELINE AND IT IS THE SAME WARNING AND NOT A NEW ONE**, a closed path is not destroyed and that is not good news, a gate coming off its hinges about nine hundred yards of a stair away is not a victory and a gate that is still held is not a defeat, being the man who went and looked is a job and not an honour and nobody was told so and nobody wrote it down, **a line with a trade on it is not a name and a paper nobody can seal is not a freedom and is not the same as a paper nobody has to obey and is not a plan, AND A PAGE THAT IS AUTHENTICATED IS NOT CONSENTED TO, AND A DOOR THAT IS OPEN IS NOT A DRAWER THAT IS OPENED, AND A ROOM THAT HAS BEEN LOOKED AT IS NOT A THING THAT HAS BEEN TAKEN OUT OF IT, AND A SMOOTH ROAD IS NOT A ROAD THIS COUNTY OWNS, AND A PLACE THAT IS STILL HELD IS NOT A VICTORY AND A DAMAGED ENGINE IS NOT A RESCUE.** A successor may not resolve any of it.

## 7. The house prose, and the six mechanical rules that are not taste

**The voice is in Chapters 0840, 0839, 0837, 0836, 0835, 0833, 0832 and 0831.** Read them before you write a sentence and match them: short declaratives, a flat cadence, a great many plain negatives used inside a paragraph and never as the frame one is built on, the census sentence where who-understood is the point, and physical work, weather, distance and a man with a bad leg everywhere else. **The dateline line carries the weekday, the market, the state of the room over the weigh-house and about four more clauses.** **The block's centre of gravity is a thing read out loud in a room, so the reading is set as work and not as prophecy: a man standing up, a sheet in two hands, nine people who hear all of it and five who do not, and the room afterwards.**

1. **Zero em dashes, zero en dashes, zero semicolons, zero exclamation marks, zero question marks, zero single asterisks and therefore no italics, zero straight double quotes and zero curly apostrophes.** Speech takes curly doubles. Apostrophes are straight. Per-line bold parity even on every line. Every file ends in a newline.
2. **One footed money column per chapter**: ten items, priced 1 to 41, a mark at forty-eight pence in every conversion, and the coda that names **some of** the figures in the chapter that are not in it, being that the list is a list of examples and not a complete inventory and a successor may not print it as complete, **and the coda may name no figure that is a price in that chapter's own column, and that was checked on every earlier block of this volume and it will take repairs here.** A figure named in that list which occurs nowhere else in the chapter is not a fault of this instrument and was recorded at `state/continuity.md` 1879 and `state/open-threads.md` 817, and **a successor who wants the list to be strict changes the instrument and then every block at once and does not do it inside one block.**
3. **THE COLLISION SET MUST BE REBUILT OVER ALL EIGHT HUNDRED AND FIFTY FILES ON DISK, MUST NOT BE INHERITED, AND MUST BE EXPECTED TO COME BACK WITH NO FREE VALUE IN IT AT ALL.** The instrument is the printed total, taken as the spelled phrase in every spelling this manuscript prints across the whole hundred band, **and every spelling means the hundreds that value prints under and to no other, being *one hundred* and *a hundred* in the one hundreds, *two hundred* in the two hundreds and *three hundred* in the three hundreds, each with the remainder written as *and* the tens or as the tens with no *and*, a bare hundred word with no number word after it reading as its own remainder of zero, plus the bare digit with a non-digit on either side of it, with a chapter heading not read as a total, run over every file whole.** **ON THE EIGHT HUNDRED AND FORTY FILES THAT STAND NOW IT GIVES 284 PRINTED VALUES IN THE BAND SIXTY TO THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE BAND, AND ZERO FREE ONES, AND NOTHING UNDER SIXTY IS FREE EITHER.** That zero is true because the ten pages of Volume 16's Batch 0005 name 266, 273 and 326 in themselves, which is a different reason from the withdrawn one and may not be re-derived back into it. **THE INSTRUMENT HAS TO BE WRITTEN OUT EVERY TIME AND IT HAS FAILED TWICE IN TWO OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS: too narrow, being an instrument that omits the *a hundred and …* spelling, returns values that are already printed; too wide, being an instrument that pairs every remainder with every hundred, counts *a hundred and sixty-six* as a printing of two hundred and sixty-six.** **AND THE CEILING OF THREE HUNDRED AND FORTY-THREE IS NOT LIFTED. Lifting it is an outline decision and `outline/volume-17.md` §7 has declined it on the page with three reasons and the third of them deciding, so this block's ten totals ARE REUSES AND THE HONEST THING TO DO IS WHAT THE LAST TWO BLOCKS' CLOSING PARAGRAPHS NOW DO: NAME THE REUSE ON THE PAGE IN THAT CHAPTER'S OWN WORDS AND GIVE THE REASON, WHICH IS ARITHMETIC, in this form: the band from sixty to three hundred and forty-three has been searched whole again and three values in it are not a value any file in the manuscript before them has printed, being two hundred and sixty-six, two hundred and seventy-three and three hundred and twenty-six, and not one of the three can be used, because the over-figure of each of them is one of the barred six, and the ten totals of these ten columns are printed already, and the reason is arithmetic, and the route below sixty is shut, because ten distinct prices cannot sum under fifty-five and every total from fifty-five to fifty-nine is printed and nothing under that is free either. Do not print that as one identical paragraph on all ten pages: the Volume 17 Batch 0001 review found that doing so puts two hundred and sixty words of bookkeeping into every chapter and a writer obeying it is copying and not writing.** The barred six are 14, 20, 26, 33, 38 and 41 and none of them may be a price, an over-figure or a printed total anywhere. Foot the column four ways and check the conversion separately from the sum, being that marks multiplied by forty-eight plus the over-figure must equal the printed total. **THE FIGURES OF THIS BLOCK'S TEN TOTALS ARE THEN CHECKED AGAINST THE EIGHT-HUNDRED-AND-FIFTY-FILE SET AND NOT AGAINST A CARRIED ONE, and if the rebuild returns zero usable free values, which it will, that is a correct answer and must not be reprinted with a withdrawn reason.**
